definitions.definition: A pure semiconductor in which the number of free electrons equals the number of holes at room temperature.
A semiconductor whose electrical properties are altered by adding impurity atoms (doping).
A semiconductor doped with pentavalent impurity, where electrons are majority carriers.
A semiconductor doped with trivalent impurity, where holes are majority carriers.
The region around a pn junction depleted of mobile charges, containing immobile ions.
The potential difference developed across a pn junction that opposes further diffusion of carriers.
Applied voltage that reduces the depletion width and barrier potential, allowing majority carrier current.
Small current due to minority carriers that flows when a pn junction is reverse biased.
A heavily doped pn junction diode that maintains a constant voltage in reverse breakdown.
Breakdown in a heavily doped junction caused by rupture of covalent bonds in a strong electric field.
Breakdown in a lightly doped junction caused by carrier multiplication through collision ionization.
Capacitance of the depletion region in reverse bias due to uncovered immobile charges.
Capacitance due to stored minority charge in a forward-biased pn junction.
A device that converts alternating current into pulsating direct current.
Ratio of the RMS value of the AC component to the DC component in a rectifier output.
The maximum reverse voltage a diode can withstand without breakdown.
A three-terminal active device in which current at one terminal is controlled by voltage at the other two.
Region where the emitter junction is forward biased and the collector junction is reverse biased, used for amplification.
Region where both emitter and collector junctions are forward biased, acting as a closed switch.
Region where both emitter and collector junctions are reverse biased, acting as an open switch.
Transistor configuration with the base common to input and output; low input and high output resistance.
Transistor configuration with the emitter common to input and output; used for amplification.
Transistor configuration with the collector common to input and output; used for impedance matching.
Modulation of effective base width by collector-base voltage, increasing collector current.
Breakdown when the collector-base depletion region extends through the base to the emitter.
Ratio of collector current to emitter current in a BJT, typically 0.9 to 0.995.
Hybrid values describing a two-port network by input impedance, reverse voltage gain, forward current gain and output admittance.

definitions.definition: A bridging impedance between two nodes can be replaced by two shunt impedances to ground.

definitions.definition: Frequency at which amplifier gain falls to 1/sqrt(2) of mid-frequency gain in the low-frequency range.

definitions.definition: Frequency interval between lower and upper cut-off frequencies.
definitions.unitTitle: Small Signal and High Frequency Analysis of BJT

definitions.definition: Amplifier with cascaded stages to increase overall voltage gain.
definitions.unitTitle: Small Signal and High Frequency Analysis of BJT

definitions.definition: Multistage amplifier using resistor-capacitor coupling between stages, suited for audio frequencies.
definitions.unitTitle: Small Signal and High Frequency Analysis of BJT

definitions.definition: High-frequency small-signal equivalent circuit of a BJT using transconductance and junction capacitances.
definitions.unitTitle: Small Signal and High Frequency Analysis of BJT

definitions.definition: Ratio of change in collector current to change in base-emitter voltage at constant collector-emitter voltage.
definitions.unitTitle: Small Signal and High Frequency Analysis of BJT

definitions.definition: A unipolar, voltage-controlled three-terminal semiconductor device whose conduction from source to drain relies only on majority carriers, modulated by the gate voltage.
A FET in which a reverse-biased pn junction controls channel width and drain current.
The gate voltage at which the channel is completely depleted and drain current saturates.
A FET with an insulated gate, also called an insulated-gate field-effect transistor.
MOSFET with no conducting channel at zero gate bias; channel is enhanced by gate voltage.
MOSFET with a built-in channel that can be depleted or enhanced by gate voltage.
FET biasing method where the source resistor provides the gate-source bias voltage.
Amplifier in which a portion of the output is fed back and combined with the input.
Feedback where the output portion is added to the input, used in oscillators.
Feedback where the output portion is subtracted from the input to stabilize gain.
Conditions for oscillation: loop gain magnitude unity and total phase shift 0 or 360 degrees.
Circuit that generates an AC output without an AC input using positive feedback.
Frequency at which the oscillator output is maximized.
Mechanical stress on a crystal produces voltage across it, and vice versa.
Circuit that produces a constant DC output voltage by reducing ripple to negligible amount.
